characters.name: In General
characters.description: All Men Are Perverts: Sex is their prime objective in just about every episode. Anti-Hero: Each of the four leads is some combination of an idiot and an asshole, though they all also have their occasional moments of kindness. Butt-Monkey: Every episode ends with one or all of the boys utterly humiliated. Cannot Talk to Women: With the exception of Neil, whose idiocy still turns off most women, all of the boys become tongue-tied when speaking to girls. For all his awkwardness, Will actually tends to fare thebestin this department out of himself, Simon and Jay. Childhood Friends: Neil, Simon and Jay have known each other for ten years by the start of the series.

characters.name: WillMcKenzie
characters.description: Affectionate Nickname: His mum calls him "Petal". Ambiguously Jewish: Is nerdy, snarky, and has curly hair, as well as saying"Chutzpah"in one episode. While his actor, Simon Bird, is not Jewish, he claims numerous people have mistaken him as having such ancestry. When he dresses up in Alan Cooper's suit and hat he even lampshades that he looks "a bit like a Hasidic Jew." Audience Surrogate: In the early episodes, he's the newest student at Rudge Park, so his narration introduces the audience to life at the school. Author Avatar: Several of the embarrassing things that happen to him are lifted directly from co-creator Iain Morris' life, such as losing out a potential chance at pulling a girl at a caravan club party due to skidding across the dance floor in his socks in a panic. Berserk Button:In any situation where he perceives unfair treatment, he tends to overreact. It always backfires.Hypocrisy is another one - for instance, in the second movie, Katie repeatedly talks about how "spiritual" she is, but then succumbs to base instincts of hooking up with arrogant, unpleasant ex Ben, even though she doesn't even like him. Will explodes with a"The Reason You Suck" Speechat both of them.

characters.name: Simon Cooper
characters.description: Aesop Amnesia: In season one, he deduces that his infatuation with Carli is either misplaced or futile. By the start of season two, he falls for her again and it's only until the movie that he realises she's a manipulator who strings him along for her own gain. The Alleged Car: His bright yellow Fiat Cinquecento Hawaii,which gets shitter and shitter just about every time it appears. Anguished Declaration of Love: Hetriesto give one to Carli practicallyOnce an Episode, but something always goes wrong. Author Avatar: Several of the embarrassing things that happen to him are lifted directly from co-creator Damon Beesley's life, such as spray painting his crush's driveway in a poorly thought out attempt at declaring his love. Be Careful What You Wish For: After spending literally the entire series chasing after Carli, in the second movie,he has a girlfriend who is a totalYanderewho ends up cheating on him.

characters.name: Jay Cartwright
characters.description: Abusive Parents: His dad belittles him in almost every conversation he has in the series and his mother just sits there and lets him. Aesop Amnesia: After causing the death of his dog Benji by lying about how the dog crapped on the carpet (leading to his dad euthanising him for being too old), you'd think it would stop Jay lying so much. Instead, he keeps doing it and blames his masturbation habits instead out of grief. All Men Are Perverts: He will make lewd comments about every woman going and sometimes, depending on how much he's drunk, make unwanted sexual advances. However, this trope is subverted whenever he meets a girl he actually cares about. Ambiguously Bi: Jay is clearly attracted to women, almost worryingly so. However, in the yearbook, created by the show's writers, in Jay's "A to Z of Sex" section, when trying to find a word beginning with "B", the word "bi-curious" is crossed out, suggesting that Jay may be bisexual or at least bi-curious. In the series itself, he has no problem with putting his hands down Will's trousers to apply hair removal cream. Finally, in the film, he starts a habit of smacking Simon in the balls whenever he mentions Carli. Animal Lover: Though it's generally buried under his attempts at seeming cool and tough, Jay is shown to have a soft spot for animals, and is genuinely remorseful when he accidentally gets his dog put down and when he runs over a squirrel.

characters.name: Neil Sutherland
characters.description: Always Someone Better:In terms of sexual opportunities, he's this to Will. ARunning Gagis that many of the girls Will fails with end up going to Neil instead.He also ends up doing very well at the newspaper job that Will was supposed to do during their week of work experience, to the point they want to keep him on, whereas Will ends up alienating everyone at the garage job Neil was supposed to go to by condescendingly saying he's too clever for a menial job.Played Within that Neil is suggested to be liked at the newspaper job preciselybecausehe's too stupid to bother asking questions to his supervisor (who implies that all of their previous work experience hires were toadying Will types) and generally keeps out of the rest of the staff's way, rather than for any actual skills he possesses. In terms of sexual opportunities, he's this to Will. ARunning Gagis that many of the girls Will fails with end up going to Neil instead. He also ends up doing very well at the newspaper job that Will was supposed to do during their week of work experience, to the point they want to keep him on, whereas Will ends up alienating everyone at the garage job Neil was supposed to go to by condescendingly saying he's too clever for a menial job.Played Within that Neil is suggested to be liked at the newspaper job preciselybecausehe's too stupid to bother asking questions to his supervisor (who implies that all of their previous work experience hires were toadying Will types) and generally keeps out of the rest of the staff's way, rather than for any actual skills he possesses. Bad Job, Worse Uniform: His job at Thorpe Park is to go around dressed in a monkey costume, which is prone to wasps getting into it, leaving him with some nasty stings. Big Eater: Leave him alone with food and hewilleat it.

characters.name: PollyMcKenzie
characters.description: Will's newly-divorced mother. She's quite popular among his male classmates (particularly Neil). Amazingly Embarrassing Parents:Will is embarrassed by some of the things she does, such as buying him a tight vest top for his birthday or letting slip about his childhood habits and ailments.In the first episode, it's revealed she told the school that Will was bullied, giving him no small amount of embarrassment and actually contributing to his ostracization even though the reason he changed schools was actually because of school fees, since they couldn't afford to keep sending Will there after the divorce. (Although it is possible Will actually was bullied and just doesn't want to admit it.) Will is embarrassed by some of the things she does, such as buying him a tight vest top for his birthday or letting slip about his childhood habits and ailments. In the first episode, it's revealed she told the school that Will was bullied, giving him no small amount of embarrassment and actually contributing to his ostracization even though the reason he changed schools was actually because of school fees, since they couldn't afford to keep sending Will there after the divorce. (Although it is possible Will actually was bullied and just doesn't want to admit it.) Brainless Beauty: As of the second movie. While she's always had acertaincluelessness, she has clearly taken aLevel In Dumbass, accidentally flashing everyone her cleavage while trying to adjust her webcam amongst other things.

characters.name: Mr. McKenzie
characters.description: Will's father, who cut off the family after sleeping with the work experience girl. He's absent from the television series, but appears in the first movie. Abusive Parents: He's distant and openly mocking towards his only child. Aw, Look! They Really Do Love Each Other: After treating Will rather poorly during their one and only scene together,he's shown tearing up with pride at the sight of a picture of him having fun on vacation with Alison at the end of the first movie. Brutal Honesty: Bluntly tells his son that he didn't invite him to his second wedding because he's awkward around other people, and does so in a way that makes it seem like he intended it to bereassuring. Deadpan Snarker: He shares Will's dry sense of humor, though since he directs all of his snarking towards Will, his son, during his one major scene, it only serves to make him seem like a massive prick.

characters.name: Kevin Sutherland
characters.description: Neil's single father, whose failed marriage, effete mannerisms and interest in badminton have caused some rumours to fly regarding his sexuality. All Gays Are Pedophiles: Jay and Simon's mockery of hisAmbiguously Gaypersonality occasionally dips into suggesting that he's a paedophile. Ambiguously Gay: Though he strenuously denies it. Catchphrase: "Oh Neil...", usually said in tones of great exasperation. Extreme Doormat: While hedoeshave a boiling point, and kicks Neil's friends out of his house when a drunk Will viciously mocks him (and later kicks Will out again when Kerry unjustly accuses him of using her for sex after he dumped her), he generally lets his son do whatever he wants due to lacking the backbone to tell him otherwise.

characters.name: Katie Sutherland
characters.description: Neil's older sister, whom the lads ogle whenever Will's mum isn't around. Aloof Big Sister: While she acts rather cold to everyone we see her interacting with, it should be noted that she and Neil barely ever speak to each other when they share a scene together. Deadpan Snarker: She tends to respond to the lads with cutting quips. Dude Magnet: Neil’s friends find her attractive and "Thorpe Park" mentions that she has a boyfriend. Ice Queen: Always come across as bored and disinterested on the occasions when she appears. Somewhat justified in that we mostly only ever see her interacting withher brotherandhis friends.

characters.name: Alan Cooper
characters.description: Simon's well-meaning but embarrassing father. He's quite fond of regaling the lads with stories of his sex life. Amazingly Embarrassing Parents: He will not shut up about his sex life. Chivalrous Pervert: He has avery strong libido, but reserves it exclusively for his wife. It actually leads to some brief relationship trouble for them when she starts to get fed up with his sex drive. The Comically Serious: OrThe Cringe Comically Seriousif you want. Whenever he goes into unnecessary details about his sex life, he often has a completely deadpan face as if he thinks mentioning his sex life is just like discussing politics. This tends to embarrass Simon even more. Generation Xerox: When Simon confesses to him about his feelings for Carli, he tells Simon that he had a similar situation with unrequited love. Of course, he then goes on about Simon's mother's sex drive, causing Simon to be sick.

characters.name: Pamela Cooper
characters.description: Amazingly Embarrassing Parents: Not to the same extent as her husband, but she can be intrusive at times and has seemingly no problem with her husband going into detail about their sex life. Closer to Earth: Overall seems slightly less tactless than Alan. Her sex drive is seemingly also not quite as outrageous as his is. Covert Pervert: She's more tight-lipped about her sex life than her husband is, but going off of his statements has nearly as much of a libido as he does. Fetish: Simon's dad lets it slip in the movie that she's aroused by the smell of sunscreen. Good Parents: On the whole, she's probably the most normal, stable, and responsible adult on the show, though Simon is hardly appreciative.

characters.name: Andrew Cooper
characters.description: Simon's snarky younger brother. Always Someone Better: What little can be seen of Andrew hints that he's far more socially adept than Simon is, being able to shrug off Simon's insults and threats. It's mentioned that Carli would attend Andrew's 16th birthday, when it's all but stated that she never hung out with Simon on his 16th. Bratty Half-Pint: He's a typical bratty little brother in the first two seasons who is constantly annoying and undermining Simon. This trope is subverted in the third season, where he's visibly hit puberty and his characterisation is more mature to match.

characters.name: Terry Cartwright
characters.description: Jay's loud-mouthed, flatulent father. Abusive Parents: Without a doubt, the worst parent on the show. He relentlessly mocks Jay for practically everything he does, which has done a number on his self-esteem and made him desperate for any kind of praise or acknowledgment. Amazingly Embarrassing Parents: A much nastier version than the parents of the other boys. His way of embarrassing Jay in front of his friends is to hurl put-downs at him and berate him constantly. Aw, Look! They Really Do Love Each Other: Has a couple of very small moments that show he has affection for his son, both in the second movie.He starts a fight with Jay's unclefor saying the same insulting things to his son as he normally does.The first thing he does upon reuniting with Jay during the end credits is give him an affectionate noogie. He starts a fight with Jay's unclefor saying the same insulting things to his son as he normally does.

characters.name: Mrs Cartwright
characters.description: Unnamed Parent: She's not stated to have a first name, with the lads referring to her as Mrs Cartwright.

characters.name: Jay's Sister
characters.description: No Name Given: She's not stated to have a first name. Unseen No More: After being mentioned once during series 1, she finally makes an appearance during the first film, albeit not for long.

characters.name: Uncle Bryan
characters.description: Terry's cousin, who lives in Australia. Jay moves in with him and his son during his gap year in the second film. The Bogan: He's just as coarse as Jay and his dad, on top of being a racist and a bully. Honorary Uncle: A variant. Bryan is Terry's cousin, making him Jay's first cousin once removed. Despite this, Jay calls him "Uncle Bryan". Jerkass: Just like his cousin Terry, he makes fun of Jay in front of his friends. Kick the Dog: Making Jay sleep in a tent in the front yard instead of letting Jay sleep in his house is our first indicator he's an arsehole.

characters.name: Mr. Gilbert
characters.description: The head of the Sixth Form stage of education at Rudge Park, and accordingly, the major authority figure in the school for the protagonists. Apathetic Teacher: In general, Gilbert is utterly switched off from life in the secondary education system, and will generally leave you alone if you leave him alone. However, as Will discovers to his cost,Sadist Teacheris what happens when you get on his bad side... The Atoner: After denying Will a chance to use the bathroom during exam time, Will ended up soiling himself. Knowing that the poor kid could have avoided this latest humiliation if Gilbert had just fulfilled his request, Gilbert makes up for this by gently escorting Will out of the exam hall without belittling him. Once his good deed is done, Gilbert goes back to mistreating Will, even bringing up the offending incident just to keep the boy humble. Berserk Button: Seems to have one about being contradicted. Will being Will, he tends to do this a lot. Big Damn Heroes: A downplayed example, since "hero" definitely doesn't seem to apply (he's mainly doing it to keep the peace rather than out of concern for anyone's welfare), but twice throughout the series he swoops in to prevent Neil from becoming a victim of "Paedo" Kennedy's attentions.

characters.name: John "Paedo" Kennedy
characters.description: Affably Evil: He's a soft-spoken and gentle-seeming sexual predator. Ascended Extra: He's a fairly minor (but memorable) character with only a few appearances in the series. The tie-in yearbook includes several sections that focus on or prominently feature him. Caught with Your Pants Down: According to Simon, one of the stories about him is that he was caught wanking to the school orchestra. It's hard to verify the story, as it apparently happened before any of the lads attended Rudge Park. Creepy Monotone: Every line out of his mouth sounds hushed and perverted in tone. Dirty Old Man: He's a middle-aged man who is constantly trying to find excuses to molest teenage boys.

characters.name: Miss Timms
characters.description: Ambiguous Situation: Rumoured to be dating Mr. Gilbert, although this is never actually confirmed. However, considering Gilbert takes Neil making a move on her surprisingly well, it's likely that they aren't a couple. Hot Teacher: Neil and Jay both lust after her. Will doesn't see the appeal. Informed Attractiveness: Will suspects that herHot Teacherstatus is due to being the youngest female teacher. Satellite Character: She gets no focus whatsoever outside of being an object of lust for Neil.

characters.name: Carli D'Amato
characters.description: Alpha Bitch: She has a much higher standing in the popularity pecking order than the lads and, especially in series 3 and the first movie, comes across as one of the most popular girls at school with a bitchy streak and apoor choice in men. Ambiguous Innocence: Since she never receives any individual focus of her own, it can be hard to get a read on just how exactly she feels about Simon. Sometimes she seems to only be interested in him for the sake of stringing him along for her own benefit, but other times she seems to be genuinely willing to hang out with him without an ulterior motive. It doesn't help that Simon himself constantly does disgusting, embarrassing, and even horrible things in front of her by mistake, giving her plenty of reason to fully dislike him. Beautiful All Along: Her profile in the yearbook hints at this having happened prior to the beginning of the series; she started to get in with the popular crowd after she got out of braces and into make-up. Big Sister Instinct: She doesn't take kindly to Will telling her little brother Chris about terrorism, stating "He won't sleep for a week now, you idiot!". Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: She comes across as aNice Girlin the first season, but knowingly strings Simon along. By the first movie, she outright uses him for her own ends.

characters.name: Charlotte Hinchcliffe
characters.description: All Girls Want Bad Boys: Was in a relationship with Donovan, and it's implied she's not totally over him. Buxom Beauty Standard: Her breasts are, according to Jay, so large and perfect that she needs specially made bras. Defrosting Ice Queen: She's seen as unattainable by the lads, but Will manages to break the ice with hiswitafter an awkward start. Even after his disaster in bed with her and his spreading of lies that they were more than they were, she's still nice to him considering. Dude Magnet: As the hottest girl in school, it’s natural that she’d have boys interested in her; the Lads (especially Will) lust after her, her ex-boyfriend Donovan still likes her, she slept with Patrice at a party, and mentions at one point that she’s taken eleven lovers. Everyone Has Standards: As promiscuous as Charlotte may be, she doesn't appreciate being treated like a sexual conquest. When she found out that Will talked about her in an objectifying manner, she snapped at him.

characters.name: Mark Donovan
characters.description: Arc Villain: Will incurs his wrath in the first episode and he antagonises him throughout the first series, punishing Will in ways such as chasing him when he tries to gets his Frisbee back, tying him to a chair with a bin over his head foran entire school day, and threatening to kill him if he tells anyone about his sensitive side or tries anything with Charlotte. It's only when he makes a beeline for Will at the Christmas prom and Big John gets the rest of the school to stand up to him, he backs down. He is still a menace to the lads after series 1, but to a much lesser extent. Ax-Crazy: Will refers to him as "the school psycho." Hash seems to make him "spread butter like a maniac." Bad Guys Do the Dirty Work: It's implied he beat upPatricefor sleeping with Charlotte. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: He has a façade of being polite in front of parents, which is why he manages to get into a lot less trouble than he should. The Bully: Donovan starts on Will on the first day and doesn't let up, even giving him a wedgie on their final day at school. He also swindles Jay and Neil in broad daylight after they offer him money for marijuana and bears down on them when they try to protest.

characters.name: Big John
characters.description: All There in the Script: His surname, Webster, is only revealed in the Inbetweeners Yearbook. Big Eater: He eats so many burgers at the Christmas prom that Will has to tell him to stop. Bullying a Dragon: His attempt to get Donovan to stop threatening Will at the Christmas party actually works. Given that he's new and a bit dumb, hemay not have even realisedthat Donovan isThe Bully. Butt-Monkey: His whole purpose is to be lower on the social pecking order than the protagonists. Fat Idiot: He's not all there and tends to get lost easily.

characters.name: Tara Brown
characters.description: A student in the year below who becomes Simon's girlfriend in Series 3. "All Grown Up" Remark: Implied by her claim that Simon only started noticing her after she "dyed [her] hair and grew a pair of tits." Characterization Marches On: In Tara's first appearance, she's a wryDeadpan Snarkerwith an interest in music and a light punk aesthetic. Once she and Simon begin dating, though, she becomes a doe-eyedGenki Girlwho considers dressing her boyfriend up like "an eccentric posh child" to be absolutely adorable. Possibly justified if you interpret her toalsobe undergoing the effects ofLove Makes You Dumbalong with Simon; becoming more flighty and nervous around her first serious boyfriend. Curtains Match the Window: Brown hair and eyes. Deadpan Snarker: In her first appearance, she's fairly witty.

characters.name: Suzie
characters.description: Child Prodigy: She's about 12 and already taking her A-levels. Redheads Are Uncool: Suzie is a strawberry blonde and belongs to the dorky clique that Will tried to break away from. Neil is horrified when he finds out she's his blind date. Also, her mum apparently escorted her on their date. Smart People Wear Glasses: She's got a pair of spectacles the size of her face and since she's taking her A-levels several years early, she can be considered one of the most intelligent characters in the whole series.

characters.name: Rachel
characters.description: Carli's closest friend. Aloof Dark-Haired Girl: She reacts to pretty much every scenario with total apathy. Give Geeks a Chance: Subverted. Rachel takes a passing interest in Will that he latches onto for the rest of the episode, only to lose interest when he nearly gets them alienated by some London clubbers. Her interest is well and truly extinguished when a suave older guy chats her up while Will gradually slips into one of his trademark hissy fits. Satellite Character: She's Carli's most prominent friend, but there's not much else to her.

characters.name: Samantha
characters.description: A rough-talking girl. Boyish Short Hair: As if to emphasise just how much like Jay she is, she sportsthe same haircut. Distaff Counterpart: She's a dead ringer for Jay both in personality and appearance. What Happened to the Mouse?: She's implied to be a friend of Carli's since they're shown getting lunch together, but she never appears outside of a single episode.

characters.name: Lauren Harris
characters.description: A Northern Irish student who enrolled in Series 2. Culture Blind: Lauren apparently went a full 16 years without once being exposed toStar Wars. Dude Magnet: In her only appearance episode-wise, Lauren ends up in aLove Trianglewith Simon and Will, and Neil calls her fit upon first glance. Foil:Unlike Carli, Lauren makes it clear she's into Simon (and not into Will) from the get-go.She also contrasts the street savvy and sexually assertive Charlotte by being a lot more innocent and thus not framed in a sexual light. Unlike Carli, Lauren makes it clear she's into Simon (and not into Will) from the get-go.

characters.name: Danny Moore
characters.description: One of the younger (and more belligerent) students. Ax-Crazy: Will assumed Danny would back off after successfully beating the tar out of Simon. Instead, he called in a gang to help him beat up Simon even harder. Catchphrase: "I'll fucking do ya!" Hair-Trigger Temper: The kid will pick a fight with anyone for no reason at all. Even after giving Simon the beating of a lifetime doesn't satisfy him, as he rounds up a posse to finish him off along with the other lads.

characters.name: Hannah Fields
characters.description: A girl from the year below who fancies Simon. Fan Disservice: The sight of a girl coming onto Simon and giving him a handjob on sight is not the least bit sexy, ranging from Hannah being clearly underage to Simon making eye contact with the other boys. Hard-Drinking Party Girl: She's at least a year younger than Simon and already chugs spirits by the bottle. Romantic False Lead: She sends Simon a Valentine's Day card but is never seen again after the Work Experience episode.

characters.name: Alistair Scott
characters.description: A student who was absent from school for a long time due to suffering kidney failure. Casanova Wannabe: Alistair makes passes at both Carli and Charlotte, with the implication being that he's going through every girl at the fashion show because he's a shallow wanker milking his illness for a pity screw. Disability as an Excuse for Jerkassery: Jay claims he was always a dick, but the stint in hospital and reliance on a wheelchair has given Alistair a visibly inflated ego. When Will gets all haughty, Alistair starts ramming his wheelchair into him. It's All About Me: While Alistair's illness does grant him the bare minimum of sympathy, it's hard to deny that he's savouring the attention far more than a sick kid with a less overblown ego would. He even gets mad at Will for trying to ruin "[his] special day" (the fashion show, which is actually supposed to be raising money for the hospital). Jerkass Has a Point: Alistair may be a dick, but he's not wrong to call out Will for trying to stage a boycott of a charity fashion event because he personally disagrees with it or tocall him a hypocriteonce he abandons his protests when Charlotte asks him to stand in for one of the models.

characters.name: Kerry
characters.description: A friend of Tara's that she tries to set up with Will. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: Kerry initially comes across as a nice girl, but when Will rebuffs her she lies to everyone saying that he was using her for sex. The Ditz: She asks Will if he needs glasses to see better... Huge Girl, Tiny Guy: Will is insanely insecure about the fact that Kerry is a head taller than him. Inelegant Blubbering: She bawls her eyes out after Will rejects her oral sex offer.

characters.name: David Glover
characters.description: One of the school's existing students when Will arrrives at Rudge Park. The Generic Guy: He's the first person outside of the new students that Will is inducted with that Will tries to talk to. As such, he isn't given much of a persona outside of being constantly vaguely annoyed. Given Name Reveal: While he has sporadic appearances throughout the first two seasons, he's not named until his final appearance in the season two finale. Recurring Extra: He turns up in several episodes with no more than one or two lines. His episode count stands at five, the same number as both Jay and Neil's dad (not counting their movie appearances) and he's appeared in more episodes than the likes of Tara or Jay's mum.

characters.name: Louise Graham
characters.description: One of the popular girls. Always Someone Better: Her party, held on the same day as Will's birthday, is easily the more popular event. Pet the Dog: She eventually allows the boys into the party, even though she doesn't really know them (which she states is the reason why she didn't invite them in the first place). She Cleans Up Nicely: The lads are shocked to see a photo of her showing some cleavage on her birthday invitations, with Simon noting that she doesn't normally look like that.

characters.name: Sadie Cunningham
characters.description: The Ghost: We never actually see her. Running Gag: Jay steals multiple items from her bag during registration — from which it can be assumed that she and Jay are in the same form group.

characters.name: Tom
characters.description: Age-Gap Romance: He's in his early 20s while Carli is still in school. Nice Guy: Whenever Tom's onscreen, he's always very approachable. Carli claims he's a bit of a dickhead behind closed doors, but she's usually in a bad mood when she says that so it's debatable how much is true. Oblivious to Hatred: Tom seems to quite like Simon, and has no idea that Simon hates him for dating Carli. Relationship Revolving Door: Carli and Tom frequently split up only to get back together again, much to Simon's chagrin. What Happened to the Mouse?: Carli gets back with Tom in the Series 2 finale. He never appears in Series 3, though Carli is out of focus in that season so it's possible the relationship fizzled out offscreen.

characters.name: "Friend"
characters.description: Nice Guy: From what little is seen of him, he seems like a very upbeat and open kind of guy. No Name Given: Nobody - not even Jay - ever uses his real name. Phrase Catcher: Simon will say "friend" in a high pitched voice when referring to this guy, knowing full well it annoys Jay. Status Quo Is God: Jay's friendship with him ends only a few days after it's revealed, as Simon needles Jay about it until Jay blows up and nearly wrecks his car in a blind rage.

characters.name: Becky
characters.description: First Kiss: Becky's the first girl Simon kisses onscreen. Foil: To the Punk Girl, being another teenage girl at the caravan club. While Becky is wholesome and sweet, the punk girl is coarse and willing to sleep around. Nice Girl: Jay sets Simon up with her because he reckons she wouldn't take him for granted like Carli does.

characters.name: Punk Girl
characters.description: Foil: To Becky, being another teenage girl at the caravan club. While Becky is wholesome and sweet, the punk girl is coarse and willing to sleep around. No Name Given: Her real name isn't established. Opposites Attract: She propositions the uptight Will before settling on Neil, who doesn't understand some of the lengthy words she uses. What Does She See in Him?: Her choice in sexual partners include the dorky Will and the dopey Neil.

characters.name: Wolfie
characters.description: Spanner in the Works: He ruins Will's chance at patching things up with Charlotte and immediately buggers off with a smug grin. Younger Than They Look: He's 17, but looks much older. Possibly from working in a garage and lack of self care.

characters.name: Patrice
characters.description: Chick Magnet: Every female character seems to be lusting after him, includingWill's Mum. He even shags Charlotte Hinchcliffe at Louise Graham's house party. French Jerk: His very first words are "I don't like Arabs" and he bluntly tells Will in English that he was fantasising about his mum as he spunked in the bathroom.

characters.name: Daisy
characters.description: Age-Gap Romance: She's a few years older than Will and they very nearly have sex. It naturally doesn't go well for Will. Hospital Hottie: In his narration, Will includes the fact that she owns her own nurse's uniform in his list of reasons she's perfect for him.

characters.name: Chloe
characters.description: Call-Back: Gets one in "Will's Dilemma", when Will makes a tasteless joke about how she made Jay cry. Jay is visibly hurt by this remark, suggesting that he has not fully come to terms with their breakup. Terry Cartwright mentions her in the first film, calling her a "hound". Informed Flaw: Jay's dad thinks she's ugly, when if anything she's out of Jay's league. Morality Pet: Jay is MUCH kinder when he starts dating her. Nice Girl: Is very sweet. When breaking up with Jay, she tries to let him down as gently as possible and wants to remainfriends. Status Quo Is God: She only dates Jay in a single episode before dumping him.

characters.name: Sophie Brown
characters.description: Deadpan Snarker: After watching Will eat her bonsai tree: "If you fancy a midnight snack, there's a spider plant in the bathroom". Does Not Like Men: She's not too happy about Simon dating Tara and the possibility of them having sex. Given how awful her housemates are, it's likely coloured her attitude towards men in general. When Tara runs screaming from the bedroom after Simon's disastrous attempts to achieve an erection, she tells Sophie that she'd been right about Simon all along. Jerkass: She spends her entire screentime being as hostile to the boys as possible. It's implied that having to share a dorm with three hooligans might have something to do with her misandristic attitude. Jerkass Has a Point: Her abrasive attitude is completely justified in that her male housemate and his mates are constantly drinking in the flat, making noise, while Simon brings Will, Jay, and Neil into the house with Will eating a bonsai tree, Jay barging into her room to try and have sex with Heike, and Neil wetting the bed withgreenpiss. And then there's also Simon's own disastrous attempt to have sex with Tara, which frightens her. No wonder Sophie threatened to call the police. Pet the Dog: She genuinely loves her sister and is very protective of her, as seen when a frightened Tara rushes into her arms after Simon turns "weird." Downplayed in that while she is by no means nicer to Will, she is slightly more tolerant of him than the other boys. She doesn't immediately throw Will out of her house for eating a bonsai tree, being more confused than anything, and she is (briefly) willing to let the boys stay after he points out that none of the boys are clothed.

characters.name: Lewis, Joe & Daniel
characters.description: Birds of a Feather: All of them loud, obnoxious and prone to bullshitting, Jay naturally hits it off with them. By the same token, Will does not. Frat Bro: They're very loud and come up with the most bizarre reasons to either chug beer or make someone else chug beer. This isTruth in Television: Whilst it isn't ALL college/uni students do all day, many do like to play drinking games, and both pointing and asking questions ARE common reasons for a forfeit drink. In-Series Nickname: They call each other The Commander, The Bombardier and The Admiral. Jerkass: They're loud, obnoxious bullshitters who take advantage of Jay and Neil's naiveté for their own amusement (e.g. telling Jay that Heike will sleep with him and daring Neil to down a bottle of orangeade with cigarette butts at the bottom). Small Role, Big Impact: It's revealed in a deleted scene that they were responsible for Jay scaring Heike by telling him that Heike would sleep with him. Jay's actions partly contribute to the boys being thrown out of Sophie's house and the breakdown of Simon and Tara's relationship.

characters.name: Alison
characters.description: Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Gone without a mention in the sequel. A deleted scene briefly reveals that her relationship with Will didn't go much farther than what we saw in the first movie. False Soulmate: She and Will seem to get together at the end of the first movie, but he's single again by the start of the second. Friends with Benefits: Offers to be this for Will after dumping Nikos.It's implied in the sequel that this was as far as it went. The Gentleman or the Scoundrel: Will being the gentleman and Nikos being the scoundrel. Give Geeks a Chance: While she has trouble admitting it (mostly due to already seeing someone at first), she likes Will enough to give him a fair chance.

characters.name: Lucy
characters.description: All Love Is Unrequited: Played straight regarding Lucy's feelings for Simon. Averted at the film's climax. Betty and Veronica: The Betty to Carli's Veronica. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: The first movie portrays her as a friendly and caring person. But in the sequel, she's quickly revealed to be an obsessive yandere and a bitch who destroys Simon's possessions out of paranoia that he's losing interest in her. And then, at the end of the film, it's revealed thatshe lost interest in Simon for someone else. Brooding Boy, Gentle Girl: With Simon, who still hasn't moved on from Carli. Devoted to You: Would do anything for Simon, despite only having just met him.She's later revealed to be insanely clingy.

characters.name: Jane
characters.description: Amicable Exes:Unlike Lucy with Simon, she and Jay part on quite pleasant terms in the second movie. Big Beautiful Woman: In spite of Jay hoping not to get stuck with her, he is secretly attracted to her and the pair of them eventually get together. She has no angst about her appearance, even coming up with better insults for herself than James manages. False Soulmate:She ends up breaking up with Jay between the first movie and the sequel and, despite his best efforts, does not get back together with him. Lonely Together: Jane and Jay are the only characters who aren't in love triangles. Motor Mouth: She's quite chatty during her first meeting with Jay, who is both too drunk and disappointed to properly engage with her.

characters.name: Lisa
characters.description: Beta Couple: Her relationship with Neil isn't given nearly as much screen-time as the others. Birds of a Feather: Is basically a clone of Neil. Brainless Beauty:Neilmanages to outsmart her. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Doesn't get so much as a mention in the sequel. Distaff Counterpart: Looks and acts like a female version of Neil.

characters.name: James
characters.description: All Girls Want Bad Boys: Provided they don't have poo on their noses. Beauty Is Bad: James is tanned, handsome, athletic…and a cruel, obnoxious bully with no redeeming qualities. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: He starts off appearing to be a seemingly friendly and laid-back guy, but is later revealed to be a complete scumbag. Failed a Spot Check: He didn't bother checking the rolled-up note Jay pried from the back of his trousers, leading to him getting a bit of poo on the tip of his nose. Faux Affably Evil: On the surface, he's pretty friendly and charismatic around others, but deep down he's a cruel and aggressive bully who gets off on other people's misery.

characters.name: Richard
characters.description: Alone Among the Couples: He's wandering around the resort on his own and ends up calling his parents when being alone causes him to have a breakdown. Cloudcuckoolander: Doesn't seem quite all there.Neillooks savvy next to him. Straw Loser: He's got no friends, has to beg for money and ends up calling his parents to come to Malia and take him home.

characters.name: Nicole
characters.description: Neil's supervisor and girlfriend. What Does She See in Him?: She's seen Neil's work ethic and has been around him long enough to see he's pretty much a child in an adult's body, but willingly formed a relationship with him.

characters.name: Nikos
characters.description: Good Adultery, Bad Adultery: Alison flirting with Will and letting him touch her naked breast isn't treated as unfaithful, but Nikos outright screwing a girl and getting caught by Alison is depicted as unforgivable. Jerkass: He cheated on Alison and tried to charm her into forgiving him, all the while his side-dish was within earshot. When that fails he punches Will, who had nothing to do with the affair. Laser-Guided Karma: After Alison caught Nikos cheating on her, she stole his ticket for the Boat Party and gave it to Will. National Stereotypes: Before even meeting him, Will correctly guesses that he's a stereotypical Greek waiter who seduces tourists, getting every single aspect of his character down pat except for his name. Straw Misogynist: Nikos clearly doesn't hold women's intelligence in high esteem, as he honestly believed he could sweet-talk Alison after she caught him being unfaithful. He also doesn't consider the feelings of the girl he was screwing, as she didn't seem to have been aware he was seeing someone else.

characters.name: Katie Evans
characters.description: A girl Will knew back at his old school who he meets in Australia. All Girls Want Bad Boys: In spite of the fact that Ben is a complete asshole, she can't help but be physically attracted to him. Bitch in Sheep's Clothing: A case could be made for this, as she's stringing Will along while carrying on with Ben in an on/off relationship, despite the fact that she despises him. When Will calls her out, she agrees to have sex with Ben within earshot of Will knowing it would agitate him. Bourgeois Bohemian: Was privileged enough to attend the same school Will went to before the series began and has a surface-level understanding of spiritualism. Character Tics: She likes to give Will friendly punches in the shoulder.

characters.name: Ben Thorton-Wild
characters.description: Bourgeois Bohemian: Will identifies Ben as a trust fund baby who is probably travelling on his parents' dime but is an utter hypocrite in his views on wealth. Hate Sink: Not as bad as James from the first film but still a pretty terrible person. He passive-aggresively dominates Will for no reason and generally acts like a smug know-it-all. Hipster: He's got the whole anti-mainstream thing going for him, especially during hisEstablishing Character Momentwhen he thinks that havingmedical supplieson a tough trek is too touristy. I Shall Taunt You: His last appearance is fucking Katie in front of Will while chanting "I don't lose". Jerkass: He berates Will for simply trying to introduce himself. Katie doesn't even like him, but can't help but be attracted to him. He's not even an in-your-faceJerk Jocklout so much as more of a university snob.
